title: Today's count is old news
hook: The report says 100 cases today. How many people were actually infected today?

knows: that cases are counted when they are reported
doesNotKnow: that reported cases are infections from days ago
that on a growing curve a delay hides a large current size

misconception: Today's reported count tells you how many people are being infected today.
objective: The learner can explain that a report counts infections from the delay ago, so with doubling every 3 days and a 9-day delay, 100 reported means about 800 infected today, and longer delays or faster growth hide more.

claims.text: If infections double every 3 days and everyone is reported 9 days after infection, today's report counts the infections of 9 days ago; 9 days is 3 doublings, so 100 reported today means about 100 x 2^3 = 800 infected today.
claims.source: Arithmetic: infected(today) = reported(today) x 2^(delay / doubling time). Computed in Demo.tsx (mult) and node.

claims.text: On the stage, a 3-day delay gives about 200 infected today, a 12-day delay about 1,600; other delays give 100 x 2^(delay/3).
claims.source: Same function draws the infection curve; arithmetic.

claims.text: On a growing curve any delay hides more of the present the longer it is; on a flat curve a delay hides almost nothing.
claims.source: infected(today) / reported(today) = growth factor over the delay, which is 1 when the curve is flat.

claims.text: The model is a made-up outbreak with steady doubling and the same reporting delay for everyone; real reporting delays vary.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx, stated on the stage before the prediction and in the reveal. Variable reporting delays: Gostic K.M. et al. (2020) Practical considerations for measuring the effective reproductive number, Rt. PLOS Computational Biology 16(12): e1008409 (verify before publishing).

recall.question: In a toy outbreak cases double every 2 days and people are counted 6 days after infection. Today 50 are reported. About how many were infected today?
recall.why: Six days is three doublings, so the infections have multiplied by 8 since the reported people were infected: 50 x 8 = 400.
